chapter: Learning drums and Roy Eldridge's band
title: Roy and Joe Eldridge; Joe's funeral
summary: Clarke recalls Roy's older brother Joe, an alto player and arranger and good teacher, and the funeral he attended after the army.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Uh-huh. And that's the year I joined Roy, and --
Well tell me, first of all, when did you and Roy first meet? Which school did Roy go to?
Well, Roy went to school on the north side.
What was the name of his school?
I don't know, really.
Oh. Was he the same age as you?
Roy? No, he was a little older, and he had an older brother.
Joe.
Joe, yeah.
Yeah.
Who really was really an extraordinary musician as far -- he was a good teacher.
An alto player.
Yes, he was an alto player and arranger.
Joe died, didn't he?
Yes. Well, I was in his funeral the last time I was home.
When?

This was -- well, let's see, I went home -- let me get it straight now. When was I home? Let's see, Joe died about -- I went out to the hospital to see him. We decided to all go out to the hospital, and when we arrived at the hospital I went up to the desk and then she said, 'Don't you know? Mr. Eldridge passed away about two hours ago.' I said, 'Well, I couldn't know, because my trip was about an hour.'
Oh, how awful.
Let's see.
Imagine that. Roy wasn't there.
Yeah, Roy was there.
You and Roy went out? Oh, he was --
Yeah, when I was home, see?
Yeah. Roy was there at --
Let's see. I'll tell you exactly when. Was it -- it was right after I came out of the army. This must
have been 1946 or '47. Oh, for heaven's sake.
And so we all went to Joe's funeral and everything.
That was sad, wasn't it.
Oh, it was very. He was really something. For me he was really --
Was he? He was very schooled, wasn't he?
Yes, very. And he --
And he wrote.
